about: What each bone rig.py makes is called on two skeletons motion often comes on: NVIDIA's SOMA (the 30 joints MotionBricks writes, github.com/NVlabs/motionbricks, motionbricks/assets/onnx/soma/soma_n1.json) and Mixamo. A motion from either can be renamed bone for bone with this table, turned into the plain form animate.py takes (how far each bone has turned from the T-pose, where the hips and feet are), and played on any character here. A tail and other extras are outside the table: a humanoid motion leaves them to follow the hips.
rest_pose: T-pose, z up, facing -y, so left (_l) is +x. Each bone's y axis runs along it; x is the bend axis.
soma_also: A joint listed under soma_also or mixamo_also has no bone of its own here: its turn is added to the bone it is listed under.

soma_unused.Jaw: no jaw bone: the low-poly face is fixed
soma_unused.LeftHandThumbEnd: hands are mittens: one bone each
soma_unused.LeftHandMiddleEnd: hands are mittens: one bone each
soma_unused.RightHandThumbEnd: hands are mittens: one bone each
soma_unused.RightHandMiddleEnd: hands are mittens: one bone each

extras: tail_1, tail_2, ... (hips > tail_1 > tail_2 ...), only on a model with a tail
